title: SLO anchoring + trace-sampling migration for analytics-metrics-service
creator: Ananya Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce trace ingestion volume and storage cost for the analytics-metrics-service while preserving the fidelity of SLIs used for metrics pipeline SLOs (ingest latency, processing error rate, export success). We will introduce an adaptive trace-sampling policy tied to traffic rate and error signals, add deterministic high-fidelity sampling for error paths, and formalize SLIs and alert thresholds. This ticket covers design, implementation, e2e tests, dashboarding, and a staged rollout with a feature flag.

Scope:
- Define SLIs for analytics-metrics-service: ingest_latency P95, processing_error_rate (5m), export_success_rate (1m).
- Implement trace sampling middleware in metrics-ingest that supports rate-based and deterministic sampling keys (customer_id, trace_id).
- Add sampling controls exposed via console feature flag and runtime config (remote-config).
- Update observability pipelines: ensure sampled traces include the minimal tag set required to reconstruct SLI calculations.
- Build dashboards and alert rules in Grafana/Alertmanager and add runbook links.
- Migrate existing tracing export to new sampling policy with canary rollout.

Non-goals: Quantization of spans, full overhaul of pipeline schema, or changing metric schemas outside of minimal required labels.
updates: 2025-02-21: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Analytics, and Backend. Agreed SLI candidates and acceptance criteria. Action: SRE to propose alert thresholds by 2025-02-25.

2025-02-24: Design doc posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CO/Adaptive+Trace+Sampling+for+Analytics-Metrics-Service. Design covers sampling modes (baseline rate, burst protection, error-force-sample) and required minimal span attributes.

2025-02-26: Prototype implemented in branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-ingest/pull/387. Prototype supports sampling-key deterministic hashing and runtime rate override. Initial micro-benchmarks show ~18% CPU increase at 1000r/s due to extra hashing; tradeoff accepted after discussion because it enables dramatic reduction in export volume.

2025-02-28: SLOs formalized and reviewed with PM and SRE: ingest_latency P95 < 300ms, processing_error_rate < 0.5% (5m), export_success_rate > 99.5% (1m). PM (Sofia Martinez) approved thresholds with condition to revisit after 2-week observation window.

2025-03-01: Added structured logging to capture sampling decisions (sampled=true|false) for downstream validation. Logs emitted to Loki with label set: service, env, sampling_mode. Logging format: JSON LTSV. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metrics-ingest/pull/402

2025-03-02: Integration tests added to CI that validate sampled traces still include fields required for SLI computation (customer_id, request_id, processing_time_ms). Test run: https://ci.redwood.ai/blue/organizations/jenkins/metrics-ingest/detail/PR-402/3/pipeline
Pending: Create Grafana dashboard panels that correlate sampling rate vs SLI drift. Dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics/sampling-vs-slos (internal draft).

Risks & mitigation: Risk of under-sampling rare error modes causing SLO blindspots. Mitigation: deterministic force-sampling for any span with error tag or status>=500 and an explicit low-latency error mirror that sends full traces for the first error per 5m per customer.
Blockers: Waiting on runtime-config rollout (ENG-11874) for remote sampling control. Dependency ticket ENG-11874 must be green for staged rollout automation.

Next steps: 1) Finish dashboard panels and alert rules, 2) Run 48h canary in staging with 10% traffic under new sampler, 3) If stable, increment to 50% then full rollout behind feature flag. Post-rollout: 14-day observation to confirm no SLI regressions.
